A1.justification: Both PDFs, including their appendices, support comparison after text extraction and visual inspection. Despite the changed title and terminology, the shared equations, experiments and retained numerical results establish that they describe the same research work.

before.justification: v8 reports original GLUE, mathematical reasoning, code generation and chat evaluations, alongside rank ablations, gradient measurements and resource benchmarks.

after.justification: v9 retains original fine-tuning results and adds synthetic adaptation experiments, timing measurements, MBPP evaluations and results for additional model configurations.

M1.justification: The DiSHA shard-sharing mechanism and Bone's efficient blockwise implementation are retained under FOSSIL terminology. However, v9 removes Bat as a defined method, including its pretrained-weight-dependent affine updates and row/column variants from v8 Section 3.5. A residual Bat mention in v9 Section 5.5 does not retain this substantial method component.

E1.justification: v9 adds synthetic sinusoidal-function adaptation and MBPP code evaluation, while removing WizardLM-Evol-Instruct chat training and reported MT-Bench evaluations. GLUE, MetaMathQA/GSM8K/MATH and CodeFeedback/HumanEval coverage remain. The MT-Bench heading in v9 Appendix Table 6 contains no results and does not establish retained chat coverage.

E2.justification: In the main generation comparison, v8's LLaMA2-7B OLoRA row is replaced by DoRA, which is also added for Mistral-7B. The new synthetic comparison in v9 Figure 2 includes AdaLoRA, DoRA, VeRA, ProLoRA, MoS and full fine-tuning alongside LoRA and PiSSA. MoRA is discussed but does not appear in that figure's evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: v9 introduces a controlled MLP protocol with 50 training samples, 100 validation samples, 250 pretraining epochs and 100 adaptation epochs, plus initialization/training-time scaling measurements. It adds LLaMA2-13B, Qwen3-4B and RWKV7-3B configurations. Existing Mistral trainable counts also change: LoRA/PiSSA from 89.1M to 94.4M and Bone/FOSSIL from 88.1M to 87.0M; these reported revisions do not establish rerunning.

E4.justification: v9 adds controlled analyses of adaptation versus computational efficiency and loss-versus-token/time comparisons. It removes the Bone-versus-Bat and Bat grouping ablations from v8 Sections 4.4–4.5, and removes FrozenFT/BigLoRA controls from the gradient analysis. The rank-performance table remains, while the gradient discussion moves from the appendix into Section 5.4 with reduced controls.

E5.justification: v8 reports two seeds for generation experiments. v9 Table 3 states three independent runs, but Section 5.2 still states two seeds, so an actual increase cannot be established. Appendix B newly specifies synthetic-experiment seed 43. The GLUE three-seed averages and accompanying uncertainty values remain unchanged.

E6.justification: v9 adds substantial synthetic, MBPP and additional-model results while removing chat and Bat result entries. Existing values also change: LLaMA2-7B Bone/FOSSIL HumanEval is 24.08 in v8 Table 2 and 23.63 in v9 Table 3. Mistral GSM8K changes from 66.94 to 68.92 with different trainable counts, preventing a same-setting improvement claim. GLUE, rank-table and retained RWKV6 resource values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The central blockwise-summation identity and efficient complexity derivation remain. v9 adds an explicit rank-at-most-N argument and divisibility assumption, specifies the repeated-row expansion with D in R^(N×k), and removes Bat's tensor formulas. Figure 5 changes the generic expansion's space bound from v8's O(dk) to O(dr), although v9 Section 4.2 still states O(dk), leaving an internal inconsistency.

C1.justification: v8 presents DiSHA, Bone and Bat as distinct contributions, including overcoming collinear updates through Bat. v9 withdraws that contribution and instead foregrounds controlled investigation of the adaptability–efficiency trade-off, FOSSIL's shared-shard implementation and scaling evaluations. The broad claims of outperforming LoRA in adaptation and efficiency remain.

C2.justification: v9 interprets the synthetic comparisons in terms of expressive-capacity costs from additional sharing and initialization costs from SVD, and adds a local-redundancy explanation for input aggregation. It removes v8's explicit shared-update collinearity limitation and detailed Bat grouping/applicability discussion. Small-rank generalization concerns and hardware limitations remain, as does a residual paragraph about Bat's resource costs.

D1.justification: v9 adds PyTorch-style pseudocode and Appendix Tables 7–9 specifying optimizer, learning rate, scaling factors, dropout, batch sizes, schedules, target modules and synthetic-data generation. OpenCompass evaluation and MATH's five-shot prompting are newly disclosed; v8 does not establish a different earlier setting. These additions substantially expand reproducibility information beyond v8's sparse settings and repository references.

R1.justification: v9 substantially repositions the work around adaptability versus efficiency, explicitly relating it to shared-parameter methods ProLoRA and MoS and discussing VeRA and MoRA. Much of v8's adapter/prompt-tuning and GQA/KV-cache background disappears. The new positioning also describes LoRA-GA and LoRA+ as largely orthogonal to FOSSIL, rather than simply motivating alternatives to LoRA.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, DiSHA/Bone terminology is consolidated into FOSSIL, and a controlled experimental section now precedes the method. Gradient analysis moves into the main text, while appendices are reorganized around additional results, settings and a checklist. Incomplete renaming and stale references remain.

P2.justification: The two-column presentation becomes single-column. Architecture graphics are replaced by a redrawn schematic with pseudocode; diagnostic and timing plots are added; retained loss and gradient plots are combined; and benchmark tables are expanded and restructured. Bat diagrams and comparison tables disappear. These are substantive display changes beyond pagination or numerical updates.

improvement.justification: Compared with v8's sparse experimental settings, v9's pseudocode and Appendix Tables 7–9 make implementation and protocols easier to assess and reproduce. The controlled adaptation/timing study also provides direct evidence for the efficiency argument. These benefits yield a limited net improvement, tempered by removed structural controls and collinearity discussion, conflicting two-versus-three-run statements, and inconsistent memory-complexity reporting between Figure 5 and Section 4.2.
